title: Check if All A's Appears Before All B's
spaceBreakdown:
- no containers allocated; only a loop index and the result of find
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input string s
approach: The string is valid iff no 'b' is immediately followed by an 'a' - i.e., the substring "ba" never occurs. Scan once looking for "ba"; if found return false, otherwise true. This is correct because any global violation (a 'b' before an 'a') forces at least one adjacent "ba" pair at the transition point.
hints: In example 2, "abab" is invalid - at which pair of adjacent indices does the ordering first break, and what are those two characters?
Use a single linear scan checking each adjacent pair for the substring "ba". In "abab", s[1]='b' and s[2]='a' form "ba", so return false immediately.

**Single character** - n=1, no adjacent pair exists
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: loop bound `i <= s.size()-1` then accessing s[i+1] → out-of-bounds read on the last index

**All b's** - no 'a' exists in the string
`Input: s = "bbb"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: requiring `count_a > 0` before returning true → returns false

**ba at start** - violation is at the very first pair
`Input: s = "ba"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: starting the scan at index 1 (`for i=1`) → misses s[0]='b',s[1]='a', returns true

**All a's** - no 'b' exists in the string
`Input: s = "aaa"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning `count_b > 0` as the validity condition → returns false

followUps.q: Generalize to any lowercase alphabet - check if the string is non-decreasing.
followUps.a: Scan adjacent pairs and return false whenever s[i] > s[i+1]. Same idea, just a character comparison instead of a fixed "ba" check. O(n) time, O(1) space.

followUps.q: Characters arrive one at a time in a stream; after each arrival report whether the prefix seen so far is valid.
followUps.a: Keep a boolean `seenB`. On each new char: if it is 'a' and seenB is already true, the prefix is invalid forever; if it is 'b', set seenB. O(1) time per character, O(1) space.

followUps.q: Answer many range queries [l, r] asking whether substring s[l..r] is valid.
followUps.a: Precompute firstB[i] (first 'b' at or after i) and nextA[i] (first 'a' at or after i) in O(n). For a query, let p = firstB[l]; if p > r the substring is all 'a's (valid), else check nextA[p] > r. O(n) preprocessing, O(1) per query.
